title: Evaluating a Deterministic Validator Plus Single‑Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=300 paired intent→configuration tasks; preregistration id cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) to evaluate whether a minimal guarded pipeline—single‑shot LLM generation (declared model: gpt-5-mini) followed by a frozen deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first‑pass misconfiguration relative to plain single‑shot generation. Execution completed 600 episodes and used 301 model calls. Observed outcomes: baseline = 299/300 valid (99.667%); guarded = 300/300 valid (100.0%); paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single permitted automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]). The preregistered planning assumption used for power calculations (planned baseline pass rate = 0.40) was contradicted by the observed near‑ceiling baseline, rendering the preregistered H1 (≥50% relative reduction) not meaningfully testable; we report the preregistered design, artifact‑grounded counts, confirmatory statistics, and artifact‑linked recommendations for future NetOps confirmatory evaluations. All run artifacts and analysis outputs are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Translating high‑level operator intent into safe device configuration is a core NetOps task. Large language models (LLMs) can produce human‑readable configuration plans quickly, but probabilistic generation risks misordering, omission, or unsafe commands. Hybrid generate→verify→repair architectures combining probabilistic generators with deterministic validators and bounded repair loops are widely proposed as operational floor‑safety nets, yet reproducible, preregistered evaluations that quantify the concrete effect of minimal guarded pipelines on first‑pass misconfiguration rates remain limited. We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped paired experiment to measure the incremental effect of a frozen deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair iteration applied to a single shared LLM candidate per task. Our core research question: does this minimal guarded pipeline reduce first‑pass misconfiguration rate relative to plain single‑shot generation under controlled paired sampling semantics? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment with deterministic seed generation and archived per‑task artifacts; (2) confirmatory inferential results computed from archived artifacts; (3) an artifact‑grounded sensitivity bound and diagnostic accounting tied to observed discordant pairs; (4) practical, artifact‑traceable recommendations for future NetOps confirmatory studies.
sections.related_work: Recent system demonstrations document promising intent→configuration synthesis in lab and testbed settings while reporting operational failure modes (misordering, omission, overconfidence) that threaten safety [10.1002/nem.2313]. Work in adjacent domains (medical QA, code repair) shows that verifier‑assisted pipelines and repair loops reduce factual errors and improve grounding, motivating similar guarded architectures for NetOps [10.36227/techrxiv.176784505.56675782/v1; 10.2139/ssrn.6608518]. Deterministic network verification techniques (header‑space analysis, specification‑based checks) provide algorithmic foundations for validators that can statically check reachability and policy constraints without live changes [10.1145/3098822.3098834]. Surveys and governance analyses emphasize auditability, provenance, and human‑oversight as practical requirements for agentic NetOps workflows [10.6028/nist.ai.100-2e2023]. Our study situates itself at the intersection of these strands by executing a preregistered, archived paired evaluation that directly measures first‑pass validity under an explicit frozen validator+bounded repair floor.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and hypotheses: The experiment was preregistered (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) before observing outcomes. Two confirmatory hypotheses were registered: H1 — the guarded pipeline reduces first‑pass misconfiguration rate by ≥50% (relative) versus single‑shot generation; H2 — one or fewer automated repair iterations recover ≥75% of initially invalid configurations. The preregistration explicitly reported the planning assumption baseline pass rate = 0.40 used for power calculations; because the empirical baseline diverged substantially from that assumption, H1 could not be meaningfully tested as a large‑effect confirmatory claim (this limitation is reported here in Methods to make the inference boundary explicit). Design and pairing semantics: paired within‑task design using a frozen deterministic task generator that produced 300 seeds; for each seed a single shared LLM candidate was generated and served as the baseline response and the starting point for guarded validation and possible repair (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Planned episodes = 600 (2 per seed), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Model, sampling, and provider policy: the declared generation model in the execution contract was gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration is execution/model_configuration.json (SHA-256: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). That artifact records the sampling parameter temperature = null; the experiment therefore did not set an explicit temperature in the recorded configuration and sampling determinism is unspecified (provider default sampling behavior applies). This unset temperature is an archival fact and may affect reproducibility under different provider defaults; we disclose it here and in the Disclosure Statement with the authoritative artifact path and hash. Validator and scoring semantics: the frozen deterministic validator canonicalized outputs to a normalized AST and applied explicit workflow/dependency checks encoded in task payloads; success required satisfying required_sequence and expected_final_state constraints plus preregistered workflow policies. Repair adapter: invoked only when the validator reported violations on the shared candidate; limited to a single automated repair attempt per episode and required to perform minimal targeted edits to remove reported violations. Statistical analysis: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Preregistered primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided (α=0.05) with paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). Missingness and retry rules, contamination detection, and deterministic exclusion/replacement policies are reported in the preregistration and enforced via the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑derived): planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; complete pairs analyzed = 300. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared initial generations + 1 repair invocation). No provider/infrastructure failures occurred under the preregistered retry policy; no deterministic contamination exclusions were triggered. Primary outcomes (archived counts): baseline_success_count = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded_success_count = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency (archived): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. These counts are reproduced in the archived analysis artifact analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55). Inferential results (preregistered): exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 1/300 ≈ 0.0033333; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Repair outcomes (H2): the single allowed automated repair corrected the sole invalid baseline output (repair success 1/1; Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]). Clarifying why McNemar p = 1.00: the exact McNemar distribution conditions on the observed discordant total (n10 + n01 = 1); with only a single discordant pair, the test has no room to produce small two‑sided p‑values for large preregistered absolute effects and yields p = 1.00 for the observed ordering (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). In this setting the absolute paired difference and the paired bootstrap CI are the primary informative summaries; both are reported above and are reproducible from the paired_contingency_table.csv and the bootstrap parameters archived in the analysis bundle. All per‑task validator traces, repair prompts/responses, and raw responses are archived and constitute the authoritative source for these extracted counts.
sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded interpretation and design diagnostics. The observed near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) contradicted the preregistered planning assumption (baseline = 0.40) and removed statistical headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction in failure rate; we therefore do not claim confirmatory support for H1. The shared_initial_candidate pairing semantics were chosen to emulate remediation of a single proposed plan (improving ecological validity for that operational question) but increase within‑pair correlation and reduce expected discordant pairs; this tradeoff should be explicitly incorporated into power calculations. Practical guidance traceable to archived artifacts: (1) calibrate task difficulty or adversarially augment the task bank to produce a planned number of initial failures (targeted discordant pairs) if the primary estimand is a large absolute/relative improvement; (2) preregister pairing semantics and repair budgets and incorporate their effect on expected discordant counts into sample‑size computations; (3) include emulation/simulation stages when runtime control‑plane/dataplane effects are relevant, and preregister how emulator outcomes map to success/failure. Validator traces (normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, repair_applied) proved diagnostically valuable for post‑hoc failure analyses and are essential archival primitives for explainable NetOps guardrails. Limitations: synthetic task bank and constrained vendor templates limit external validity; single declared LLM and a single validator implementation restrict generality across models and validator designs; repair evidence is based on a single corrected case (wide CI).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (N=300 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation (declared model gpt-5-mini) with a guarded pipeline composed of a frozen deterministic validator and a single automated repair iteration. Baseline single‑shot generation yielded 299/300 valid outputs and the guarded pipeline yielded 300/300 valid outputs; the one observed baseline failure was corrected by the single permitted automated repair. The preregistered H1 target (≥50% relative reduction) relied on a planning assumption (baseline pass rate = 0.40) that the observed data contradicted; therefore H1 was not meaningfully testable in this run and no confirmatory claim of H1 is made. The archival artifacts constrain inferential possibilities (observed discordant pairs = 1 → maximal resolvable absolute paired difference = 1/300 ≈ 0.00333) and directly support the numerical summaries reported above. Future confirmatory NetOps evaluations should (a) align task difficulty and adversarial augmentation to produce required initial failure counts for targeted estimand precision, (b) preregister pairing semantics and repair budgets explicitly, and (c) add emulation when runtime semantics are material. All raw outputs, validator traces, repair traces, analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived and enumerated in the Disclosure Statement for reproducibility and audit.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor‑template scope limit external validity to diverse production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

The preregistered power plan assumed a baseline pass rate = 0.40; the observed baseline (299/300) contradicted that assumption and removed headroom to detect the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction.
Sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate) reused the same initial candidate across paired arms, increasing within‑pair correlation and reducing discordant pairs available to McNemar inference.

Validation used deterministic static configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; actual runtime consequences (control‑plane convergence, transient reachability) were not executed and remain unmeasured.

Repair‑success evidence is based on a single initially invalid case (1/1 → 100%), yielding a wide Clopper–Pearson 95% CI = [0.025, 1.0]; larger counts of initial failures are required to estimate repair effectiveness precisely.
